title: sales-partnership-scratch-notes-lena-rodriguez
content:
Account: Nimbus Data Solutions (target prospect)
Date: 2025-02-10 (notes + outbound drafts)
Owner: Lena R.

Quick context / why them
- SMB / mid-market analytics company that builds embedded analytics for vertical SaaS (healthcare, finserv).
- Heavy emphasis on latency-sensitive features (real-time transcription, chat help).
- Public blog + job posts show hiring for ML infra + vector search expertise => likely evaluating inference infra options.
- Likely current stack: AWS (EKS + S3), Postgres, some Redis. Using open-source LLMs internally per engineer tweets (small models for POCs).
- Pain: costs for serving at scale, reliability during peak usage, security/compliance in healthcare customers.

Primary value props to emphasize
- Predictable per-token economics + configurable dedicated capacity (helps their cost predictability for customer billing).
- Private deployment / VPC option for healthcare customers + KMS integration.
- Smart routing / fallback for reliability during peak loads (reduce incidents).
- Observability (token-level cost + latency traces) to attribute feature costs to product teams.

Account intelligence (people to target)
- CTO: Maya Thompson (hiring ML infra + wrote blog about latency for inference)
- Head of Product: Jorge Alvarez (owns developer-facing SDKs)
- Director, Platform Eng: Keisha Martin (manages infra + deployment options)
- Security lead: Daniel Wu (HIPAA oversight)

Warm signals / where we saw them
- Tweet thread (Jan 2025) complaining about inference cost spikes with open model endpoints.
- Job listing: "Senior ML Infra Engineer" mentioning quantization/serving experience.
- Customer case study page mentions "real-time" analytics for healthcare.

Outbound email drafts (A/B test)
1) Short cold (subject: 2 lines)
Subject: Reduce inference spend for real-time analytics
Hi Maya — quick note: I saw Nimbus’s recent post about real-time analytics and wanted to share how Redwood helps teams lower per-token cost while keeping sub-100ms tail latency (dedicated pools + batching + KV caching).
If you’re open, 15 min to see a simple cost/latency comparison vs your current setup?
— Lena

2) Product-led angle (subject: try dedicated capacity)
Subject: Dedicated capacity for consistent SLAs (15 min?)
Hey Jorge — we help product teams give customers consistent latencies by pinning model versions to dedicated GPU pools. We’ve helped similar customers reduce incidents from traffic bursts and simplify billing to customers.
Can I share a short case study and a custom rollout plan?

3) Security-first angle (subject: HIPAA + VPC options)
Subject: HIPAA-ready inference in your VPC
Hi Daniel — saw Nimbus serves healthcare customers. Redwood Private offers VPC/on-prem deployments + KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs — everything your security team will ask for during an RFP.
Would love to introduce our security brief (2 pages) and set up a sync with your security lead.

Call script (15 min intro)
- 0:00–1:30 intro (1-liner: "Redwood builds inference infra so product teams can ship LLM features with predictable cost and latency")
- 1:30–4:00 ask about current stack and pain ("how are you currently serving models in prod? biggest reliability/cost headaches?")
- 4:00–8:00 show quick micro-case: dedicated capacity + routing to lower incidents and cost (high level numbers only: 30–50% cost reduction for some workloads; elide vendor names)
- 8:00–12:00 discuss security & private deployment if healthcare customers are on roadmap
- 12:00–15:00 agree next steps: tech deep-dive (30–45m) + share cost baseline info (ask for token counts / QPS)

Objection handling (short snippets)
- "We host everything on AWS managed endpoints" => "Totally common — Redwood runs on top of cloud infra but adds serving runtime + batching/kv caching and observability; many teams keep infra but switch to our runtime for better unit economics. We can do a small PoC to compare."
- "Not ready to talk security/hipaa" => "No problem — we can share our HIPAA whitepaper and do a separate session with security. Many folks start with a non-sensitive workload POC."
- "We already have a dedicated GPU setup" => "Great — are you happy with utilization and rollout controls? We can help with autoscaling policies and model rollout tools that many infra teams find saves ops time."
- "Cost savings sound too optimistic" => "We usually do a two-week baseline PoC with your traffic (or replay) — we’ll instrument same metrics and show real delta before any commit."

Notes-to-self / ask for ENG collaborator
- Samir to share cost model template + sample case study numbers for real-time chat workload (need 95th p99 latencies and per-token cost ranges).
- Ask Solutions Eng (Olivia) if we have a one-pager targeted to healthcare + HIPAA + VPC deployment.

Follow-ups / next actions
- Send Email A to Maya + Jorge (track opens).
- Attach HIPAA brief for Daniel + ask for security lead intro.
- Prep short case study: "SaaS analytics co reduced inference spend by 37% with dedicated pools" (get numbers from Samir).
- If any reply: 15 min intro + ask for token counts/QPS for baseline PoC.

Misc scratch ideas (brainstorm)
- Quick template: "cost-latency delta" one-pager: small table (baseline vs Redwood: p50/p95/p99 lat, cost per 1k tokens, ops hours saved).
- Could run a small benchmark playbook vs AWS endpoints using public model to show realistic numbers (coordinate w/bench infra team).

End of notes.

Unresolved questions:
- Do we have a HIPAA-specific architecture diagram I can share? (If not, ask infra/security)
- Who on SE side owns healthcare vertical? (Olivia?)
